newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 23.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Saturday ruled out snap polls over a leadership tussle in the Congress party widely expected to determine the fate of his six-month old minority government.
Local agencies quoted Deve Gowda as telling businessmen in the southern state of Karnataka they need not worry about the stability of his government which he said would complete its five-year term.
"I am not worried about it. You are worried about it," the United News of India quoted Deve Gowda as telling reporters earlier when he was asked if the Congress crisis could trigger snap polls.
** Indian industrial growth will slow to eight percent in 1996/97 (April-March) handicapped by falling demand, high borrowing costs and political uncertainty, business leaders said on Sunday.
India has targetted industrial growth of 12 percent for the fiscal year ending March 31, after notching a 12.1 percent growth rate in 1995/96.

** Higher rural incomes and recent cut in the cash reserve ratio (CRR) by the Reserve Bank of India are likely to boost demand and spur investment activity in the economy, the Financial Express reports.
Quoting a study done by stock brokerage James Capel B&K, the paper says the recent CRR cut would lead to a fall in interest rates apart from increasing consumption expenditure.

** India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index rose to 6.88 percent in the week ending Dec 7 from 6.80 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.

Scattered profit-taking is expected to halt rebounding Indian stock markets in the holiday-shortened week because traders would not want to keep open positions during the Christmas vacation, analysts said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange and most other bourses in the country are open only on Monday and Tuesday this week.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's top-30 stock index jumped 228.54 points, or nearly 8 percent to 3,110.19 last week.
